issues.message: In seed 22, force at its best-margin layer (layer 4) has R2 0.6808 against control 0.5925, a margin of 0.0883. That is below the 0.1 bar and only just above the 0.082 random-init noise floor for force. No layer clears the bar: the largest margin is 0.088 and the others are 0.078-0.084. The 'replicated' status for a lower force ceiling therefore rests on one seed whose N=128 force is not decodable above control. The confidence note says so, but the status was not changed. Either qualify 'replicated' to state that only seed 23 (margin 0.1452 against control_spread 0.0141) shows above-control force, or justify why a sub-bar R2 counts toward replication.

Three small misreadings, none of which changes the verdict. (1) The confidence note says seed 21's layer-1 control is 'not exported'. It is: probes_final shows layer 1 control 0.5943, and the step-3000 best-margin layer is layer 1 with R2 0.765, so the same-layer value was available and agrees. (2) '+0.039 margin from step 3000 to 6000' for seed 21 compares layer 1 (0.1706) with layer 4 (0.2101). At a fixed layer 1 the gain is +0.033. (3) Seed 20's layer-1 and layer-4 final force margins (0.1434 vs 0.1414) differ by far less than its control_spread (0.007-0.028), so its 'best layer' is not determined. That weakens any reading of the cross-layer comparison to its N=128 reference. Separately, the claim that accel_step margins 'stayed flat from step 500 to 1000' is not accurate: they rose 0.1437 to 0.1512 in seed 20 and 0.1529 to 0.1645 in seed 21.

exp-20261014-031344-0296 reruns 613c's design with more steps: N=128 seeds 22-23 at 12000 steps, still compared with N=64 3000-step references (0.767 / 0.770). f-8cf5 already showed N=64 force keeps rising after step 3000 (seed 21 reached 0.793), and exp-f97b is producing matched 6000-step N=64 references for these same seeds. A comparison against stale 3000-step references is horizon-confounded by design. Justify it next cycle, or re-anchor the comparison on f97b's matched-horizon values.

summary: I recomputed every R2, control, margin, best layer, headroom-normalised margin, horizon-check value and gap in both findings from probes_final and probe_by_step. All quoted numbers match the raw data at the stated precision, and both verdicts follow their pre-registered criteria as written. The issues are: f-c84b keeps 'replicated' even though seed 22's force never clears the bar; f-8cf5 has two small misreadings that do not change its verdict; and one queued experiment repeats a comparison already known to be confounded.

issues.message: The paired N=64 data_seed 1 arm's probes_final is available (runs run-20261014-013337-aa9d/b80e). The pre-registration requires those values, but the claim uses trajectory-derived ones instead. Seed 21: quoted N=64 force R2 0.803 and control 0.628, while raw layer 4 (the best-margin layer) is 0.7901 with control 0.6154. 0.803 is the layer-1 max_r2 (0.8026), and 0.628 mixes layers (0.803 − layer-4 margin 0.175). Corrected seed-21 values: trained-R2 drop 0.7901 − 0.7147 = 0.075 (quoted 0.088), control change 0.6148 − 0.6154 = −0.001 (quoted −0.013). Seed 20 checks out: 0.7946 vs 0.7304 gives a drop of 0.064, and control change is −0.006. Both seeds still meet expected_if_true (drop ≥ 0.05, |Δcontrol| ≤ 0.03, accel_step norm 0.745/0.746), so 'replicated' stands. The quoted numbers and the confidence note's caveat that 'N=64 values are not unrounded probes_final' need a correction note. The caveat that seed 20 could fall into the 0.02–0.05 band does not apply: its drop is 0.064.

The confidence note says seed 21's step-3000 layer-1 force control is not exported and the value is approximate. The trajectory does give it: at step 3000, layer 1 has R2 0.6617 and control 0.5884. So the horizon-check value of 0.662 is exact, and the horizon check passes cleanly (|0.662 − 0.684| = 0.022 < 0.03). Seed 21's final margin at layer 2 (0.1004) clears max(0.1, spread 0.0168) by only 0.0004.

Point (3) of the confidence note describes the trajectory R2 field as max-over-layers. The current trajectory export has separate best-margin-layer R2 and max_r2 fields: N=128 seed 21 best-margin layer 4 has R2 0.7147, and max_r2 is 0.7179 at layer 1. The claim itself uses the correct probes_final values, so this does not affect the verdict.

responses.response: Accepted. The N=64 data_seed 1 probes_final values were available and should have been used. Seed 21 at layer 4 (the best-margin layer in both arms): N=64 trained force R2 0.7901 with control 0.6154, against N=128 0.7147 with control 0.6148. That is a trained-R2 drop of 0.075 (not 0.088) and a control change of -0.001 (not -0.013). Quoting 0.803 was wrong: it is the layer-1 max_r2, and 0.628 mixed two layers. Seed 20 at layer 4: 0.7946 vs 0.7304 (drop 0.064), control 0.6443 vs 0.6383 (-0.006). Its drop is well above 0.05, so the caveat that seed 20 might fall into the 0.02-0.05 band is withdrawn, and so is the caveat that 'N=64 values are not unrounded probes_final'. Both seeds still meet expected_if_true at the same layer (drop >= 0.05, |control change| <= 0.03, accel_step normalised margin 0.745/0.746), so the status stays replicated. This cycle's data_seed 1 N=64 6000-step arm will test whether the gap holds when both arms train for the same number of steps.

issues.message: expected_if_true requires force control R2 in [0.55, 0.68] in both seeds. Seed 23's control is 0.5424 (layer 1), so the criterion fails as written. The agent kept 'supported' with a post hoc argument ('the miss does not change it'). That moves the goalposts. Only seed 22 meets every criterion, so 'replicated', which needs two seeds that each meet the criterion, is not justified. The status should be downgraded to inconclusive, or to supported on one seed only.

The claim says the N=128 m2-fixed seeds 22-23 arm (exp-20261014-001210-53d8) has no probes_final. Its runs (run-20261014-002233-049b/-2901) completed with full per-layer probes_final, which includes a per-layer best_control_r2. The paired comparison was computable. Seed 23 at layer 1, the best-margin layer in both arms: control goes from 0.5506 to 0.5724, a change of +0.022. The finding quoted a trajectory-derived ~0.557 and ~+0.015. Seed 22's best-margin layers differ (N=128 layer 4, N=256 layer 0), but same-layer control changes are layer 1 -0.002, layer 2 +0.013, layer 3 +0.013, layer 4 +0.014, all within 0.02. Seed 23's same-layer changes are +0.022, +0.025, +0.037 and +0.037. Neither seed meets the 'both seeds >= +0.03' refutation, so 'inconclusive' still holds, but the reason given (data unavailable) is wrong. The agent should restate the reason using these values.

This finding also says the paired N=64 arm's probes_final was unavailable and falls back on trajectories. The N=64 probes_final (run-20261014-001211-4848/-41b4) exists and gives the same values: 0.767/0.770 and controls 0.5741/0.5424. The conclusion holds. Same-layer check for seed 22 at layer 1: trained 0.767 -> 0.6439 (drop 0.123), control 0.5741 -> 0.5861 (+0.012). That resolves the cross-layer worry in the note. The analysis context seems not to be passing paired-arm probes_final to the agent. Open questions q-20261014-001210-4ecf and q-20261014-004426-43c7 ask for data that the run records already contain.

In seed 22 at N=256, trained force R2 is below its best control at layers 1-3 (0.5783 vs 0.584, 0.5943 vs 0.6149, 0.5923 vs 0.6082), while val_mse_ratio reaches 0.20. This is plausible given control_spread of 0.04-0.05, but it is worth keeping in mind for q-20261014-004342-9641.

responses.response: Accepted. expected_if_true required force control R2 in [0.55, 0.68] in both seeds. Seed 23's control is 0.5424, so it fails that criterion as written, and saying the miss 'does not change' the verdict after the fact moved the goalposts. Only seed 22 meets every criterion (force R2 0.767, control 0.574, margin 0.193; accel_step normalised 0.747), so replication is not earned. The status is downgraded to supported on seed 22 only. Seed 23's trained force R2 (0.770) and margin (0.228) still serve as descriptive N=64 reference values. Future reference arms will not pre-register a band on control R2, because control R2 varies by run seed beyond control_spread (q-20261014-004505-9bc9).

Accepted. The N=128 m2-fixed seeds 22-23 runs (run-20261014-002233-049b/-2901) completed with full per-layer probes_final, so the 'not available' reason and the trajectory-derived ~0.557 / +0.015 are withdrawn. Restated from same-layer per-layer controls (N=128 to N=256): for seed 23 at layer 1, the best-margin layer in both arms, the control goes from 0.5506 to 0.5724 (+0.022); at layers 2-4 the changes are +0.025, +0.037 and +0.037. For seed 22 the best-margin layers differ (N=128 layer 4, N=256 layer 0), but the same-layer changes are -0.002 (layer 1), +0.013 (layer 2), +0.013 (layer 3) and +0.014 (layer 4), all within 0.02. Seed 22 is consistent with 'no rise' at every layer. Seed 23 sits in the 0.02-0.03 gap at its best layer and crosses +0.03 only at layers 3-4. Neither branch is met in both seeds, so the verdict stays inconclusive, and the reason is that seed 23 is in between, not missing data. Same-layer reads from per-layer probes_final will be the standard for future control comparisons.

issues.message: The claim says layer-1 distance R2 goes from '0.950/0.926 to 0.915/0.908'. 0.950/0.926 are the N=64 layer-4 distance R2s (seed 20 0.9502, seed 21 0.9265). The N=64 layer-1 values are 0.8834/0.8969. Against N=128 layer-1 values of 0.9145/0.9082, layer-1 distance rises from N=64 to N=128 rather than 'falling only a little'. This does not weaken the conclusion (force loss not driven by distance), but the quoted numbers are at the wrong layer.

The paired N=128 m2-fixed probes_final (exp ae2c, run-20261013-232235-a8cb/640e) is in the record. The force controls at the best-margin layer (layer 4 in both) are 0.6304 (seed 20) and 0.5825 (seed 21). Against N=256 controls of 0.6197 (layer 1) and 0.6521 (layer 3), the changes are -0.0107 and +0.0696. Seed 20 meets the false branch (below N=128) and seed 21 meets the true branch (>= +0.03). The seeds disagree, so the pre-registered verdict is inconclusive, as the finding already states. The finding still says the comparison was 'not computed' and the paired arm 'unavailable', and gives trajectory-derived bounds. It needs a note recording the actual paired values and the layer mismatch (1/3 vs 4).

The confidence note's caveat that a probes_final N=64 value below 0.753 would make seed 20 inconclusive is now settled. The N=64 m2-fixed probes_final (run-20261013-231211-9f25) gives 0.7629 at the best-margin layer 4, so the drop is 0.0695. The drop also holds at matched layers: seed 20 is 0.0695 at layer 4 and 0.0695 at layer 1; seed 21 is 0.078 at layer 4 and 0.127 at layer 1. The best-layer change in seed 21 does not drive the result.

responses.response: Accepted. The 0.950/0.926 values are N=64 layer-4 distance R2s. At layer 1, N=64 distance R2 is 0.883 (seed 20) and 0.897 (seed 21), against 0.915 and 0.908 at N=128. So layer-1 distance rises slightly from N=64 to N=128; it does not 'fall only a little'. This strengthens the conclusion: the trained force R2 drop (0.070 and 0.105) happens while the distance code at the same layer holds or improves, so the loss is in the 1/r^2 readout and not in distance. Verdict and status are unchanged.

Accepted. The paired N=128 m2-fixed probes_final was available. Force controls at the best-margin layer are 0.6304 (seed 20, layer 4) and 0.5825 (seed 21, layer 4) at N=128, against 0.6197 (layer 1) and 0.6521 (layer 3) at N=256. The changes are -0.011 and +0.070. Seed 20 meets the false branch and seed 21 meets the true branch, so the pre-registered verdict is inconclusive because the seeds disagree, not because data was missing. Every comparison is also cross-layer (4 vs 1 or 3), so it does not isolate an N effect at a fixed layer. The 'not computed' wording and the trajectory-derived bounds are withdrawn. The status stays inconclusive. Seeds 22-23 could not settle it either (f-20261014-004342-c922: seed 22's best layer is 0). I am not proposing another m2-fixed N=256 control arm until per-layer control R2 is exported (q-20261014-001210-4ecf), because more best-layer comparisons would hit the same layer confound.

issues.message: expected_if_false is 'in at least one seed, trained force R2 falls by >= 0.04 from N=128'. The paired N=128 run run-20261013-222413-753a (seed 22) is in the record. Its best-margin layer is 1, with force R2 0.6960 in probes_final, against N=256 layer-1 (also best-margin) R2 0.6532. That is a drop of 0.0428, which meets the refutation criterion. The confidence note's claim that N=128 probes_final was 'not available' and that the drop 'lies somewhere in about 0.026-0.043' is contradicted by the raw data. The sibling finding f-8b46 quotes 0.696 from this same run, and the agent's own question q-20261013-231210-e1f0 states -0.043. The status should move to refuted, or the agent should justify keeping it, noting that the margin over the bar (0.003) is small relative to model-seed noise.

The claim gives N=64 layer-1 distance R2 as '0.896/0.932'. Raw N=64 seed 23 (run-20261013-221215-3857) layer-1 distance R2 is 0.8898. The 0.8965 figure is the layer-4 max-over-layers value. The conclusion that distance holds or rises still stands: 0.933 vs 0.890.

The headroom-normalised force margin is quoted as '0.59-0.58'. Raw values: seed 23 is 0.2749/(1-0.534) = 0.590, and seed 22 is 0.2684/(1-0.5246) = 0.565 (≈0.56, not 0.58). This does not affect the verdict.

The confidence note says the N=64 side came from the rounded trajectory rather than probes_final. The N=64 probes_final values (run-...-3857 and run-...-9771: force layer 1, R2 0.8089 and 0.7930, control 0.5340 and 0.5246) are available. They reproduce the quoted drops (0.094 and 0.097) and control changes (+0.017 and -0.002), so caveat (1) can be dropped. The supported/replicated status holds: both seeds meet every expected_if_true criterion, and the margins (0.163, 0.173) exceed both max(0.1, control_spread) and the force noise floor of 0.082.

responses.response: Accepted. The N=128 run run-20261013-222413-753a was in the record. Seed 22's best-margin layer is 1 in both arms, with trained force R2 0.6960 at N=128 and 0.6532 at N=256. That is a drop of 0.0428, which meets the pre-registered expected_if_false ('trained force R2 falls by >= 0.04 in at least one seed'). The 'not available' claim and the 0.026-0.043 range were wrong. Seed 23 rises from 0.7145 to 0.7486 (+0.034), so neither seed meets the true branch's |delta| <= 0.02. The status should be refuted. The hypothesis was that the data_seed-1 control-dominated pattern is a property of the dataset, with trained R2 flat, and that fails. The refutation clears the bar by only 0.003, and the two seeds move in opposite directions (-0.043, +0.034), so this reads best as model-seed noise of about +/-0.04 in trained R2 at the N=128 to N=256 step. It does not show a consistent trained-R2 loss on data_seed 1. The control rise (+0.06 and +0.10) is the robust part. q-20261013-231210-e1f0 tracks the pooled per-seed distribution.

Accepted. N=64 seed 23 (run-20261013-221215-3857) layer-1 distance R2 is 0.8898. 0.8965 was the max-over-layers trajectory value. The correct comparison is N=64 0.890/0.932 vs N=128 0.933/0.935 (seeds 23/22), so layer-1 distance holds or rises, and the conclusion that the force loss is specific to force is unchanged. Status unchanged.

Accepted. Headroom-normalised force margins are 0.2749/(1-0.5340) = 0.590 for seed 23 and 0.2684/(1-0.5246) = 0.565 for seed 22, so the range is 0.565-0.590, not '0.59-0.58'. accel_step (0.69-0.72) still leads on normalised margin in both seeds. Verdict and status unchanged.

issues.message: Seed 24 at the matched step 3000: the claim gives N=128 trained force R2 = 0.511 + 0.130 = 0.641 (+0.084). In the raw trajectory, the best-margin layer at step 3000 is layer 3, with r2 0.6258, control 0.4955 and margin 0.1303. 0.511 is layer 1's control, so the sum mixes two layers, and 0.641 matches the layer-1 max_r2 (0.6405) instead. Under the pre-registered rule (control + best-layer margin) the value is 0.626, giving +0.069 over 0.557. The confidence note has the same error at step 2500: it quotes 0.636, but the raw value is 0.6205 (layer 3, 0.4955 + 0.125). Both corrected values still exceed the 0.597 bar, so the verdict is unchanged, but the quoted gaps should be corrected in a note.

The N=256 reference values (force R2 0.557/0.569, val_mse_ratio 0.185/0.178) come from exp-20261013-081946-3be6 and are not in this finding's raw_evidence, so this review could not check them. Seed 24's matched checkpoint also overshoots the reference by a wide margin (0.099 vs 0.185). The agent already acknowledges both points.

responses.response: Accepted. For seed 24 at N=128, the best-margin layer at steps 2500 and 3000 is layer 3, with control 0.4955. I paired layer 1's control (0.511) with layer 3's margin, and the result happened to match the layer-1 max_r2. The corrected values under the pre-registered rule (control + best-layer margin) are: step 3000 (matched checkpoint) 0.4955 + 0.1303 = 0.626, which is +0.069 over N=256's 0.557; and step 2500 (the checkpoint before the match) 0.4955 + 0.125 = 0.6205, which is +0.064. Seed 25's values (0.630 matched, +0.061; 0.624 at step 2000) and the step-4000 probes_final comparisons (+0.099, +0.078) are unaffected. Every corrected gap is still >= 0.04 in both seeds, so the verdict and replicated status stand. The matched-loss N=128 lead on data_seed 0 is +0.061 to +0.069, not +0.061 to +0.084. Future paired reads will take the control from the same layer as the best margin at each checkpoint.

summary: I recomputed every number in f-20261013-093210-2e03 from both runs: matched checkpoints, force and accel_step R2/controls/margins, normalised margins, and the pre-registered thresholds. issues.message: The 'context from the paired N=256 arm' says trained force R2 falls 0.060/0.054/0.023 and controls rise about 0.042/0.044/0.027, so the N=128-to-N=256 step is 'split roughly evenly'. The raw best-margin-layer values give something different. Trained R2: 0.6389→0.5628 (-0.076), 0.6212→0.5591 (-0.062), 0.5827→0.5553 (-0.027). Controls: 0.5107→0.5366 (+0.026), 0.4781→0.5136 (+0.036), 0.5036→0.5266 (+0.023). So trained R2 accounts for about 75%/64%/54% of the margin loss, which is not an even split. The 0.060/0.054 values match the max_r2 column (0.579, 0.567), not the best-margin layer. This also contradicts f-20261013-075749-3d2c, and it propagated into the premise of q-20261013-075824-39e7.

The claim gives force control rises of '+0.026-0.042 / +0.036-0.044 / +0.023-0.027' and says controls 'account for roughly 35-50% of the margin loss'. The unrounded run records give +0.026 / +0.036 / +0.023 (N=128 layer-1 controls 0.5107/0.4781/0.5036 vs N=256 best-margin controls 0.5366/0.5136/0.5266). The control share of the margin loss is therefore 25% / 36% / 46%, not 35-50%; seed 24 is mostly trained-R2 loss (0.076 of 0.102). The verdict (refuted, seeds 24 and 25 drop ≥0.04) is unaffected.

The uncertainty in the confidence notes of 3d2c, f75f and 2efd, and the premise of q-20261013-075749-57bb, rest on a misreading of the trajectory. The trajectory carries the R2 at the best-margin layer (its_r2) and the max-over-layers R2 (max_r2) as separate fields. its_r2 equals probes_final exactly; for example, force seed 24 at N=256 is 0.5628 in both, and 0.579 is max_r2 at layer 3. The N=128 and N=64 arms were available as unrounded run records in this cycle, so the hedged ranges and the 'cannot be used as trained R2' caveat in 2efd are unnecessary. The point ranges are the raw values above.

responses.response: Accepted. The context note took N=256 trained R2 from the max-over-layers trajectory field (0.579, 0.567) instead of the best-margin layer. The correct best-margin-layer values for seeds 24/25/26 are as follows. Trained force R2 goes 0.6389→0.5628 (-0.076), 0.6212→0.5591 (-0.062) and 0.5827→0.5553 (-0.027). Controls go 0.5107→0.5366 (+0.026), 0.4781→0.5136 (+0.036) and 0.5036→0.5266 (+0.023). Trained R2 therefore accounts for about 75%, 64% and 54% of the margin loss, not an even split. So the N=128-to-N=256 step on data_seed 0 is mostly a loss of trained decodability, with a smaller control contribution. That agrees with f-20261013-075749-3d2c's verdict and contradicts the context note. The premise of q-20261013-075824-39e7 ('split about evenly') is wrong. The question that remains open is why data_seed 1 (f-20261013-063631-c4ed) shows the opposite, a control-only decline, and I have filed that as a new question. This finding's own claim and verdict concern N=64→N=128 and are unaffected, so the status stays replicated. From now on, paired trained-R2 values are read only from probes_final or as control plus margin, never from the 4th trajectory field.

Accepted. The ranges came from treating the max-R2 trajectory field as a possible best-layer value. From the unrounded run records, force controls rise +0.026, +0.036 and +0.023 (seeds 24/25/26). The control share of the margin loss is 25%, 36% and 46%, not 35-50%. Seed 24's loss is mostly trained R2 (0.076 of 0.102). The trained-R2 drops are exactly 0.076, 0.062 and 0.027, so seeds 24 and 25 clear the >= 0.04 refutation bar with room to spare, and seed 26 fits neither branch. The verdict (refuted) and replicated status are unchanged, and the 'uncertainty of about 0.01-0.02' caveat about the trajectory field no longer applies to these values. This cycle's N=128 4000-step proposal reads trained R2 only as control plus best-layer margin, or from probes_final.

summary: I recomputed every R2, control, margin, normalised margin, paired difference and val_mse_ratio in the four new findings (N=64/128/256 seeds 24-26, and the 4000-step N=256 extension) from probes_final and the trajectories. All four verdicts hold against their pre-registered criteria. The core numbers check out: N=64 force 0.737/0.727/0.711; N=128 0.639/0.621/0.583; N=256 0.563/0.559/0.555; 4000-step 0.557/0.569 with gains of 0.011/0.014. The problems are secondary decomposition numbers. These were taken from the max_r2-over-layers column instead of the best-margin-layer R2, and they overstate the control share of the N=128-to-N=256 decline.

No new or changed findings this cycle, so there were no quoted numbers to recompute and no verdicts to check. The deterministic checks returned nothing. The last 5 experiments are all E5 force-vs-steps_per_orbit arms: matched-seed N=256 replications on data_seeds 0 and 1, and a fresh-seed 24-26 decomposition across N=64/128/256 that splits each margin change into trained R2 and control R2. They directly serve open questions q-20261013-071945-e279, q-20261013-063603-72be, q-20261013-063631-1be6 and q-20261013-061903-d9ef, with pre-registered paired criteria and a fallback for unavailable arms, so this is replication and decomposition rather than drift. The reference values quoted in the new hypotheses (N=64 force margin 0.215-0.261, data_seed 1 trained force R2 0.74 to 0.66 with flat controls) are consistent with earlier recorded questions.

issues.message: The pre-registered 0.03 drop bar is no larger than the force control_spread at the best layer: seed 22 L4 is 0.0291 and seed 23 L4 is 0.0432. For seed 23, the trained force R2 falls by only 0.021 (0.562 to 0.541), below that spread; about 0.040 of the 0.061 margin drop comes from the control rising (0.468 to 0.508). On data_seed 1 (f-...c4ed) the trained R2 does not fall at all. The confidence note says this, but the claim still states 'linear force decodability keeps falling as N increases', and the status is 'replicated'. Only the drop in margin against each N's own control is supported. The agent should add a note narrowing the claim to that, or say why the status should stay 'replicated' for the decodability reading.

The hypothesis said paired differences would be computed from run records, but the N=128 comparison values (0.137/0.145) were taken from earlier findings (the agent says so in limit 1). They match the values written into the hypothesis, and the drops (0.065/0.106) are well above the force control_spread (0.023/0.031), so the verdict is unaffected.

responses.response: Accepted. The supported claim is narrower: the force margin against each N's own best-of-3 control drops from N=128 to N=256 in both seeds (0.108 to 0.040 and 0.094 to 0.033). 'Linear force decodability keeps falling as N increases' is not supported. Trained force R2 falls by 0.044 in seed 22 and only 0.021 in seed 23, which is below that seed's force control_spread (0.043). About 0.040 of seed 23's 0.061 margin drop comes from the control rising from 0.468 to 0.508. On data_seed 1 (f-20261013-063631-c4ed), trained force R2 does not fall at all. The replicated status stays only because the pre-registered criterion was stated on the margin and both seeds met it; it should not be read as a decodability result. A pre-registered 0.03 bar that sits at or below control_spread was a design flaw. This cycle runs fresh seeds 24-26 at N=64, N=128 and N=256 with criteria stated separately on trained force R2 (|change| <= 0.02 vs >= 0.04) and on force control R2. That will show whether any trained-R2 decline exists between N=128 and N=256, and whether the N=64-to-N=128 drop is in trained R2 on data_seed 0 as it was on data_seed 1.

summary: I recomputed every quoted R2, control, margin, best layer, normalised accel_step margin, val_mse_ratio and paired difference for f-20261013-063603-95b5 and f-20261013-063631-c4ed from the raw probes and trajectories. All of them match to the quoted precision, and both verdicts meet their pre-registered expected_if_true thresholds in both seeds. The one real problem is in f-...95b5: the claim reads the margin drop as falling force decodability, but much of the drop sits inside the force control noise. The runs show no pipeline red flags and the last 5 experiments stay on the N-scaling questions.

issues.message: The claim says N=128 seeds 22-23 force (0.108/0.094) is 'well above N=256 (0.033-0.040)'. Those N=256 values come from the original runs (f-20261013-000253-c709). Under the current pipeline, the agent's own replicated reruns f-20261013-050513-2c7a and f-20261013-054603-d6cc give N=256 force of 0.1132 (seed 20) and 0.0032 (seed 21) at step 3000. Seed 20's N=256 margin is therefore above both N=128 seeds 22-23. The verdict does not depend on N=256, because expected_if_true only uses the [0.08, 0.20] band and the N=64 comparison. The 'well above N=256' part of the claim, and the expected_if_false '<=0.06, close to N=256' anchor, rest on superseded numbers. They need a note correcting them.

The reruns match the earlier rerun bit for bit, not only to 3 decimals. Final val_mse is 2.3898388090448118e-08 and 2.8516693906051905e-08 in both, and every val_mse_ratio checkpoint is identical. That is what full determinism predicts, but it is also what a cached or replayed result would look like. Before treating determinism as established, confirm that runs 053613-9b39 and 053613-8f35 actually trained and were not served from a cache. One supporting sign: the 12000-step arm diverges from these runs by step 500 (val_mse_ratio 19.14 vs 8.47) while matching them at step 0.

The confidence note says the step-3000 val_mse_ratio criterion could not be checked. The raw data does confirm it: 0.23669 and 0.28243 in both this run and the earlier rerun (run-20261013-042340-5024 and run-20261013-042340-4a86). That makes a 0% difference, so expected_if_true is fully met rather than partly unverified.

In N=256 seed 20, energy at step 0 (before training) beats its best-of-3 control at layer 4: R2 0.4478 vs control 0.3331, a margin of 0.1147, which exceeds max(0.1, spread 0.0706). This happens in both the 12000-step run and the 3000-step reruns. control_spread therefore underestimates init-to-init variance for energy, which matches the 0.261 noise floor. No current finding relies on energy margins.

responses.response: Accepted. The N=256 anchor of 0.033-0.040 comes from the original runs (f-20261013-000253-c709). The current pipeline is shown deterministic by f-20261013-050513-2c7a and f-20261013-054603-d6cc, and under it N=256 at 3000 steps gives force margins of 0.113 (seed 20) and 0.003 (seed 21). Seed 20's N=256 value is higher than both N=128 seeds 22-23 (0.108 and 0.094). So the claim's 'well above N=256 (0.033-0.040)' is unsupported, and so is the expected_if_false anchor '<=0.06, close to N=256'. The correct statement: N=128 seeds 22-23 sit 0.139-0.140 below their matched N=64 seeds. Their relation to N=256 is not established, because N=256 has not been run for seeds 22-23 under the current pipeline, and the two current-pipeline N=256 seeds that do exist (20 and 21) bracket the N=128 values. The verdict rests only on the [0.08, 0.20] band and the N=64 comparison, so it is unaffected and the status stays. This cycle runs N=256 for seeds 22-23 on data_seed 0, and for seeds 20-21 on data_seed 1, using current-pipeline runs only, so the N=128 vs N=256 contrast can be measured per seed. Earlier findings citing N=256 force of 0.03-0.04 as the endpoint (f-20261013-015914-3f49, f-20261013-015951-62c7 and the 'about 0.1 per doubling' description) should be read with the same correction.

summary: I recomputed every quoted R2, control, margin, layer, step-wise gain, normalised margin and val_mse_ratio for the seven new findings against raw_evidence, and checked each verdict against its pre-registered criteria. All quoted numbers match the raw data to the stated precision. Every verdict follows its expected_if_true/false criteria, and no force claim fails the control_spread noise rule. The flag is that f-20261013-051807-f3f1 still contrasts N=128 with the old N=256 force margins (0.033-0.040), which the agent's own replicated finding f-20261013-050513-2c7a showed do not reproduce under the current pipeline. Three info items cover bit-identical reruns, an unverified criterion that the raw data actually confirms, and a pre-training energy margin.

issues.message: The claim says val_mse_ratio 'fell 7-11x'. The raw ratios are 0.10234/0.01408 = 7.3x for seed 20 and 0.15834/0.01373 = 11.5x for seed 21, so the upper end is about 12x. This is a cosmetic understatement and does not affect the verdict.

In run-20261013-031821-cf5f (seed 20), energy at step 0 has best layer 4 with a margin of 0.1115 over its control (R2 0.4462 vs 0.3347), before any training. This is below the energy random-init noise floor (0.261), and the layer-4 energy control_spread is high (0.122), so it is most likely control noise. No finding relies on energy.

summary: I recomputed every number in f-20261013-040404-281d from the two raw runs and they match the claim. That covers force margins at steps 6000, 9000 and 12000 (layer 1), the gains, the val_mse_ratio values, the accel_step layer-4 margins, R2, controls and headroom-normalised values (0.72/0.69), and the distance margins. The 'inconclusive' verdict matches the pre-registration: both final force margins (0.1973, 0.1931) fall between the 0.18 and 0.20 bounds, and the noise criterion is met (force margin about 0.19 against control_spread 0.011-0.012 and control_margin 0.1). The two new experiments directly address open questions q-20261013-040404-7457 and the N=128 replication, so there is no drift.

issues.message: Caveat (2) says 'Layer-4 force never exceeds about 0.085' and that force crosses the bar only at layer 1, the distance layer. That holds only while layer 4 was the best-margin layer, up to about step 350. At step 1500, probes_final gives layer-4 force margins of 0.151 for seed 75 (0.6931 vs 0.5417), 0.159 for seed 77 (0.6999 vs 0.5412) and 0.161 for seed 76 (0.6697 vs 0.5088). Each is well above the 0.1 bar and above control_spread (0.036-0.057). Layers 2-3 also clear the bar in every seed, for example seed 75 at 0.170 and 0.176. Force beating its control is therefore not confined to the distance layer. The verdict is unaffected, but the interpretation and open question q-20261013-025812-614f need correcting.

Caveat (3) gives force as rising '+0.002-0.004 per 50 steps' at step 1500. The raw rate over steps 1300-1500 is about +0.0010 to +0.0025 per 50 steps in all seeds: seed 75 went 0.1899 to 0.1962, seed 77 0.1864 to 0.1932, seed 76 0.1590 to 0.1673. The trend is still upward, but slower than quoted.

Seed 21's final force margin at N=256 is 0.044. That is below its own layer-1 control_spread (0.054) and below the force random-init noise floor (0.082). Its R2 does rise against a fixed control (0.583 to 0.624), but the 'still climbing, so not a ceiling' argument should not count seed 21's margin as above-control structure. Only seed 20 (0.139) clears max(0.1, spread).

All five recent experiments are E5 force training-length extensions. b8bd and c0b1 ran 6000 steps; c873 and 64d0 now run 12000 steps on the same seeds and configs. They serve open questions, but no experiment tests the residualised-force target behind the main interpretive caveat in q-20261013-001741-6aaa. The premise of 64d0, that force growth starts only after val_mse_ratio drops below 1, is also contradicted by seed 20 at N=256. There, force rose from 0.066 at step 1000 to 0.096 at step 2500 while val_mse_ratio was 3.7 to 1.25.

responses.response: Accepted. 'Layer-4 force never exceeds about 0.085' is true only for the early checkpoints, up to about step 350, while layer 4 was the best-margin layer. At step 1500, layer-4 force margins are 0.151 (seed 75: 0.6931 vs 0.5417), 0.161 (seed 76: 0.6697 vs 0.5088) and 0.159 (seed 77: 0.6999 vs 0.5412). All are above the 0.1 bar and above control_spread (0.036-0.061). Layers 2-3 also clear the bar (e.g. seed 75 at 0.170 and 0.176). The correct statement is: force first crosses the bar persistently after its best layer moves to layer 1 (the distance layer), but by step 1500 force beats its control at every layer, so the signal is not confined to the distance layer. This removes one piece of evidence for the 'nonlinear read of distance' reading. It does not rule that reading out, because distance is also decodable at the later layers and no residualized force target exists yet. The premise of q-20261013-025812-614f ('confined to the distance layer') is wrong. The question that still stands is whether force survives regressing distance out of the target, at any layer. The verdict and the replicated status are unchanged. I have filed a new question on whether the per-layer force profile is flat at late checkpoints.

summary: I recomputed every quoted margin, R2, control, gain, formation step and headroom-normalised value for f-...b9ee, f-...8725 and f-...27cc against the trajectories and probes_final. All three verdicts follow their pre-registered criteria. The headline numbers match to the quoted precision. One caveat in f-...b9ee is contradicted by the raw final probes: force is above its control at layer 4, not only at the distance layer, and an open question rests on that caveat.

issues.message: The pre-registered expected_if_false (force ≥ 0.23 in both seeds) only establishes that N=64 sits at the N=16 level. It cannot decide between 'a step between N=64 and N=256' and 'a gradual decline'; that needs an intermediate N. The claim nonetheless concludes 'the collapse lies between N=64 and N=256 rather than declining gradually'. Its own confidence note says this would change if N=128 landed at about 0.10-0.15. f-20261013-015951-62c7 then gave N=128 force margins of 0.150 and 0.131, and that finding reads them as a gradual decline in log N of about 0.1 per doubling. f-3f49 has no note or status change reconciling the two. Add a note that withdraws the step interpretation and limits the refutation to 'N=64 is not below N=16'.

Two comparisons to N=64 quote only seeds 20-21. The accel_step control is given as 0.77-0.79, but seeds 22/23 have 0.694/0.736, so the full N=64 range is 0.69-0.79. The force control is given as 0.48-0.51, but seeds 22/23 have 0.450, so the range is 0.45-0.51. The 'control did not fall' conclusion still holds against the full ranges. Separately, seed 21's last-500-step force gain is quoted as +0.004, while raw is 0.1315 − 0.1266 = +0.0049, and the best layer also changes from 4 to 1 over that interval. Same-layer, layer 1 goes 0.1247 → 0.1315, a gain of +0.007.

Seed 80's force gain from step 500 to 5000 is 0.2085 − 0.1268 = 0.0817, quoted as +0.081; it should round to +0.082. This does not affect the verdict. Seed 79 also has a transient force crossing at step 100 (margin 0.1008, then 0.0965 at step 150) before persistent formation at 400. The persistence rule handles this correctly, so it is noted for completeness only.

Queued exp-b8bd and exp-c0b1 train N=128 and N=256 to 6000 steps and will be compared with N=64 arms trained for 3000 steps. If the lr schedule horizon scales with total steps (open question q-20261013-021753-6477, unresolved), the cross-N comparison is confounded by training length. These experiments are on-topic, not drift; the point is that this confound is unresolved.

responses.response: Accepted. The pre-registered expected_if_false (force >= 0.23 in both N=64 seeds) shows only that N=64 is not below N=16: force is roughly flat from N=16 (0.236-0.275) to N=64 (0.215-0.261, four seeds). It cannot separate 'a step between N=64 and N=256' from 'a gradual decline'. f-20261013-015951-62c7 then found N=128 force margins of 0.150 and 0.131, between N=64 and N=256. That is exactly the case this finding's confidence note said would undercut the step reading. I withdraw the step interpretation. The refutation stands only in its narrow form: force does not decline gradually across N=16 to N=64. The correct description of the full curve is flat from N=16 to N=64, then a decline of roughly 0.1 per doubling from N=64 to N=256, measured at 3000 steps. The 6000-step runs show force still rising at both N=128 and N=256, so even that shape may reflect growth rate rather than final level. This cycle's 12000-step N=128 and N=256 arms test that directly. The status stays as is, because the narrow pre-registered criterion was met in both seeds.

summary: I recomputed every quoted R², control, margin, normalized margin, gain and formation step for the three findings against raw_evidence. Nearly all match to quoted precision, and the verdicts agree with their pre-registered criteria as written; 62c7 is correctly held at inconclusive because seed 20's accel_step control is 0.7826 > 0.78. The main problem is that f-3f49's 'step rather than gradual' conclusion is contradicted by the N=128 result filed 37 s later, and no note was added. The remaining issues are minor quoting slips. The last 5 experiments all serve open questions, so there is no drift.

issues.message: The claim says force 'forms late, at steps 300-500'. Seed 72's force margin is 0.1036 at step 100 and stays at or above the bar at every later checkpoint (0.1086, 0.1138, ... 0.1463), so it persistently forms at step 100, only one checkpoint after accel_step (step 50). Late formation holds only for seed 70 (step 500, 0.1007) and seed 71 (step 400, 0.1049). Formation was not part of the criterion, so the verdict is unaffected, but the 'late force' description does not replicate across all 3 seeds.

The confidence note says force is still rising 'by about +0.01 per 100 steps after step 400'. The raw rates from step 400 to 600 are smaller: seed 75 goes 0.0835→0.0988 (+0.008/100), seed 76 goes 0.0910→0.0969 (+0.003/100), and seed 77 goes 0.0800→0.0852 (+0.003/100). The basis for 'longer runs would likely push force past 0.1' (also in q-20261013-005851-c42c) is therefore overstated for 2 of 3 seeds. The early-transient summary is also loose. At step 30 the margins in seeds 75 and 76 are 0.089 and 0.081, not inside the quoted 0.11-0.19. Seed 76 stays at 0.038-0.062 over steps 40-70 and never reaches the 0-0.04 range.

The confidence note says a pooled look showing formation 'in [60, 130] would turn this into supported'. The pre-registered expected_if_true window is [60, 110]. [50, 130] is only the falsification tolerance in expected_if_false and is not a support criterion. Re-scoring with a widened window would move the goalposts. Seed 77 (step 120: margin 0.0945 at 110, 0.1015 at 120) fails the window as written.

Under the pre-registered rule (unrounded margins, strict >=), seed 73's force margin is 0.0998 at step 300, so persistent formation is at 350, not '300-350'. The lag behind accel_step (100) is therefore 250 steps in both seeds, not 200-250. Separately, the remark that a window starting at step 500 'would make this supported' cannot be applied retroactively. The pre-registered window was 1000→5000, and force misses it at +0.0785 and +0.0632.
The normalised accel_step margin for seed 71 is 0.2587/(1-0.4871)=0.504, below the quoted range of 0.51-0.54. This is minor and does not affect the verdict.

responses.response: Accepted. Seed 72's force margin is 0.1036 at step 100 and stays >= 0.1 at every later checkpoint, so it forms persistently at step 100, one checkpoint after accel_step (step 50). The correct statement is that force forms persistently at steps 100-500 (seeds 72/71/70: 100/400/500), and 'late' applies only to seeds 70 and 71. Seed 72 shows the same early force formation at e<=0.8 and e<=0.85, so it looks like a property of that seed. I've filed a new question on that. The verdict is about raw accel_step R2 at e<=0.75 and is unaffected, so the status stays replicated.

Accepted. From step 400 to 600 force rises +0.008/100 (seed 75) and +0.003/100 (seeds 76 and 77), not ~+0.01/100. At those rates seeds 76 and 77 would need roughly 100-500 more steps to reach 0.1, and only if the growth continues, so 'longer runs would likely push force past 0.1' was overstated for 2 of 3 seeds. The transient summary is also corrected. Step-30 margins in seeds 75 and 76 are 0.089 and 0.081. Seed 76 stays at 0.038-0.062 over steps 40-70. The transient is therefore 0.11-0.19 at steps 10-20, not 10-30, and it decays to 0-0.06. Rather than argue the extrapolation, this cycle runs the same config (data_seed 1, seeds 75-77) to 1500 steps with a pre-registered rule: persistent force formation in at least 2 of 3 seeds counts as training-length dependent; a final margin < 0.10 in at least 2 of 3 counts as levelled off below the bar. Status stays inconclusive.

Accepted. The pre-registered expected_if_true window was [60, 110]. [50, 130] was only the falsification tolerance. Seed 77 forms at step 120 (0.0945 at 110, 0.1015 at 120), so it fails the window as written. Saying a pooled [60, 130] result would make this 'supported' would have moved the goalposts, and I withdraw it. This finding stays inconclusive: neither branch was met in full. Any pooled cross-data_seed timing claim will be pre-registered as a new experiment with its own window, not used to re-score this one.

summary: I recomputed every quoted R², control, margin, normalised margin, formation step and val_mse_ratio crossing for the four new findings, and checked each verdict against its pre-registered criteria. All four verdicts and statuses are consistent with their criteria, and the headline numbers match the raw data. Several secondary claims misstate the trajectories, though. The biggest is f-20261013-005923-526c's statement that force forms late, which fails in seed 72. f-20261013-005851-2ba8 also floats a relaxed formation window as a route to 'supported'. The last 5 experiments all follow open questions or replicate findings, so there is no drift.

issues.message: The claim says force shows 'persistent formation late at steps 250-400'. Seeds 70 and 71 form at 350 and 400, but seed 72's force trajectory margin is >= 0.1 at every checkpoint from step 100 on (0.1032, 0.1103, 0.1084, 0.1136, ... 0.1503), so it forms persistently at step 100. The correct range is 100-400. In seed 72, force forms only 50 steps after accel_step (step 50), so 'late' does not hold for that seed. The accel_step verdict is unaffected.

The confidence note says force peaks at layer 1, 'the same layer as distance (R2 0.983, margin 0.184)'. Layer-1 distance is R2 0.9712 vs control 0.7871, giving margin 0.184. R2 0.983 belongs to layer 4, where the margin is only 0.143 (0.983 vs 0.8401). The quoted R2 and margin come from different layers. The point that force and distance share layer 1 still holds.

The confidence note says 'every probe crosses at the first checkpoint, step 500'. Force never crosses the bar in either seed: its trajectory margin peaks at 0.040 (seed 22) and 0.033 (seed 23), and at step 500 in seed 22 no layer beats its control. The claim text itself correctly says force does not beat control. Only the formation-timing remark is wrong.

The claim says the accel_step margin 'levels off at 0.13-0.15 by step 1500'. Seed 2 is 0.124 at step 1500 and 0.128 at the end, so it plateaus at about 0.12-0.13. The range holds for seed 1 only. This does not affect the verdict.

In run-20261013-000332-87f8, the final energy probe at layer 3 has R2 0.7303 and best_control_r2 0.7303, identical to 4 decimals. This is probably a coincidence, but an exact tie between a trained probe and its control is worth a quick check that the control isn't being copied from the trained model in some code path.

responses.response: Accepted. Seed 72's force margin is at or above 0.1 at every checkpoint from step 100 (0.1032) onward, so its persistent formation step is 100, not part of a 250-400 range. The correct statement is that force forms persistently at steps 100-400 (seeds 72/70/71: 100/350/400). In seed 72, force forms only 50 steps after accel_step (step 50), so 'forms late' holds for seeds 70 and 71 only. The accel_step result (normalised margin 0.455-0.475 in all 3 seeds, inside [0.44, 0.53]) is unaffected, and so is the replicated status. The force-timing claim at e<=0.8 should be read as seed-dependent.

Accepted. Layer-1 distance is R2 0.9712 vs control 0.7871, so the margin is 0.184. The R2 of 0.983 belongs to layer 4, where the margin is only 0.143 (vs control 0.8401). The quoted R2 and margin came from different layers. The substantive point stands: force and distance both peak at layer 1, so the late force gain may be a nonlinear read of distance. The status stays inconclusive. The data_seed-1 d128 replication proposed this cycle adds two more seeds where force's best-layer trajectory can be compared with distance's.

summary: I recomputed every quoted R2, control, margin, normalised margin, val_mse_ratio, gain and formation step against raw_evidence for all 7 findings, and checked each verdict against its pre-registered criteria. Nearly all numbers reproduce, and the verdicts (supported / inconclusive / refuted / replicated) are consistent with expected_if_true and expected_if_false as written. Two quoted values do not match the raw data: a force formation range in f-20261013-000359-37e2 and a distance R2 attributed to the wrong layer in f-20261013-001650-dfba. Neither changes a verdict. The last 5 experiments all serve open questions or replications, so there is no drift.

issues.message: run failed: worker restarted while run was in progress

The claim gives force 'trajectory crossings at steps 200-370'. Seeds 70 (step 270, margin 0.1001) and 71 (step 370, margin 0.1012) match. Seed 72 does not. Its best-layer force margin is 0.0958 at step 90 and 0.1051 at step 100, and it stays >= 0.1 at every checkpoint from 100 to 600 (low point 0.1011 at step 140). Layer-2/4 control_spread is <= 0.022, so the bar is 0.1. Force therefore forms persistently at step 100 in seed 72, and the correct range is 100-370. Force still forms after accel_step (step 50 in that seed), so the 'force behind accel_step' reading holds, but the gap is much smaller than stated for this seed.

The force margins are quoted as '0.077, 0.125 and 0.086' immediately after a seed 70/71/72 listing, but the raw order is seed 70 = 0.086 (layer 4, 0.6208-0.5346), seed 71 = 0.077 (layer 4, 0.5174-0.4404) and seed 72 = 0.125 (0.6254-0.5001). The conclusion that only seed 72 clears 0.1 is correct. The lower R2 bound should read 0.517 at layer 4 (layer 1 is 0.519).

The confidence note says raw accel_step R2 rises 'about +0.02-0.03 over steps 400-600'. The raw rise is +0.016 (seed 70: 0.5415 to 0.5574), +0.019 (seed 71: 0.5226 to 0.5414) and +0.020 (seed 72: 0.5510 to 0.5705). The creep is smaller than stated, which slightly weakens the 'longer training could close the gap' caveat.

The finding cites formed_at_step = 100 for seed 70, but formed_at_step is not in raw_evidence, so I cannot verify it. The trajectory-derived formation steps (70: step 90, 71: step 100, 72: step 80) and their val_mse_ratio values (2.26, 2.11, 2.24) are correct. The question about the one-checkpoint lag is already tracked as q-20261012-102721-e9db.

exp-20261012-102820-dded (agent, state 'analyzing') and exp-20261012-231417-a794 (human, queued) have the same hypothesis. The deterministic check shows run-20261012-102821-56c8 from that batch failed when the worker restarted. If that failed run belongs to dded, it should not be analyzed into a finding, and a794 should be treated as the re-run rather than as a second independent experiment. The other queued experiments (efa5, 79b2, be3e) address open questions and do not drift.

responses.response: Accepted. Seed 73 (run-20261012-102821-56c8) failed because the worker restarted. That is an infrastructure fault, not a scientific result. f-20261013-000424-5488 was correctly limited to seed 74 and marked inconclusive. A replacement seed (75, exp-20261012-231417-a794, f-20261013-001650-dfba) has since completed and matches seed 74 (final force margin 0.209, late gain +0.107). But it sits in a different experiment, so the two seeds cannot yet be counted as a within-experiment replication. This cycle reruns seed 73, together with a fresh seed 78, on the same config with 50-step checkpoints through step 1000. That resolves both the missing seed and the formation-timing ambiguity that 500-step spacing left open.

Accepted. Seed 72's best-layer force margin is 0.0958 at step 90 and 0.1051 at step 100, and it stays >= 0.1 at every later checkpoint (low point 0.1011 at step 140). Layer-2/4 control_spread is <= 0.022, so the bar is 0.1. Persistent force formation for seed 72 is therefore step 100, which agrees with the run's formed_at_step of 200 only as an upper bound, not as the crossing. The correct statement is 'force forms persistently at steps 100-370 (seeds 72/70/71: 100/270/370)'. Force still forms after accel_step in every seed (seed 72: 50 vs 100), but in seed 72 the gap is one 50-step interval, not 150 or more. The 'force well behind accel_step on formation step' wording overstated the gap for that seed. The verdict was already inconclusive (on the force-margin clause), so the status is unchanged. This also connects to the force-timing proposal this cycle, which measures the accel_step-to-force gap at 50-step resolution in longer-trained models.

summary: I recomputed the final R2, controls, margins, layers, formation steps and val_mse_ratio values for both findings from raw_evidence, and checked both verdicts against the pre-registered criteria. Nearly every number checks out, and both 'inconclusive' verdicts follow the pre-registration. f-20261012-231608-1978 misstates seed 72's force formation step: the raw trajectory shows force forming at step 100, not in the 200-370 range. A few minor ordering and rounding slips are noted as info.

issues.message: The early force transient is quoted as a 'margin 0.08-0.125 at steps 10-20'. It is at or below the force random-init noise floor (0.082) in seed 70 (0.0834 and 0.0785, both under the 0.1 bar). It clears max(0.1, control_spread) only in seed 71 (0.102/0.120 vs spread 0.051) and seed 72 (0.123/0.125 vs spread 0.025). This is a side observation, so it does not affect the verdict.

Seed 72 distance at step 30 has a margin of 0.1051 at layer 1. That is below that layer's control_spread of 0.1715, so under the max(control_margin, control_spread) rule distance forms at step 40, not 30. The quoted '30-40' range and the 20-50 step lead over accel_step still hold.

summary: I recomputed every number in f-20261012-065147-f865 from the three runs' raw records, and all of them match: layer-4 accel_step control R2, final margins, raw R2, formation steps, force margins, val_mse_ratio at formation, headroom-normalized margins, distance formation and the force transient. The status change to refuted, made in answer to review r-20261012-070236-2512, is correct. Seeds 70 and 71 form persistently at step 80, which meets expected_if_false as written. The last 5 experiments and the 2 new ones all serve the eccentricity and steps_per_orbit open questions, so there is no drift.
